A separate git worktree for phase 69 was created off origin/main, ready for the user to kick off in a new session.

repo: gsd-tools query commit routinely reports commit_failed even when the commit actually lands in git log — must verify with git log rather than trusting the tool's return code (recurs across multiple commits in this session).

Executor agents in this GSD setup tend to prematurely mark REQUIREMENTS.md items [x] when only part of the acceptance criteria (e.g. new facade code) is done but deletion of legacy services is deferred to a later plan/wave — orchestrator must audit and revert these before they mislead coverage gates.

worktree.baseRef config controls whether executor worktrees fork from live HEAD ('head') or 'fresh' origin/main; must be checked before dispatching worktree executors, since PLAN.md files only exist on HEAD.
Web executors touching packages that depend on @cipherbox/sdk must rebuild the SDK dist before typecheck — cross-package staleness is a known landmine in this monorepo.

Plan 06 (web owned-read rewire) surfaced that far more components (~15+ importers across apps/web/src) consume the SealedChildRef/ResolvedChild data than the 5 originally flagged — Plan 11's deletion of kind-cache/useFileSize/etc. will be blocked until all importers, including several currently unowned by any plan (utils/fileTypes.ts, lib/crypto/key-wrapping.ts, vault-settings.store.ts, TextEditorDialog.tsx, useStreamingPreview.ts), are migrated.

The UI capability plan:pre gate can report block:true at the lower ui-plan-gate check level while never actually firing, because the registry's 'when' condition classifies the phase (e.g. architecture/refactor) as not requiring the UI hook — only fires if a UI hook is active in activeHooks.
Intel API-SURFACE extraction can return 0 symbols for this monorepo; treat as empty/HINT-only and omit from planner prompt rather than pass as noise.
gap-analysis.plan-post check output can contain control chars that break the standard parser — running the check directly bypasses this.

code.finding: RotationHighWater.enforceResolved gate added to root node resolve path (resolvePublishedNode) as part of ROT-07 anti-rollback enforcement on the SDK's own read path.
enforceResolved gate also added inside dfsFindFolder's child loop; pre-existing write-path gate remains at line 1156.

resolveChildren docstring documents that per-child resolve/unseal failures are skipped (availability tradeoff) rather than failing the whole listing, because the target folder is already gated via ensureFolderLoaded/dfsFindFolder before this runs — an unverifiable sibling is simply omitted, never rendered with stale/attacker content.

workflow: When pausing mid-wave execution, let the in-flight sequential executor finish and commit atomically rather than killing it, to avoid leaving the shared working tree dirty/half-committed.

ScheduleWakeup delaySeconds must be computed from a freshly-fetched current timestamp immediately before the call — computing it earlier and using it after a session/quota gap silently produces a wake time far later than intended (25 min off in this session).

There is no clean way to retract/cancel a previously scheduled wakeup once quota resets and the user says to just continue — the stray wake firing later is harmless since session context persists, but it can't be un-scheduled.

For a pnpm monorepo where most waves in a phase are single-plan, sequential execution on the main tree can be deliberately chosen over parallel git-worktree execution to avoid repeated expensive pnpm installs and orchestration fragility, while preserving correctness via file-disjoint same-wave plans.

Independently re-running acceptance/security tests after an executor self-reports 'PLAN COMPLETE' (rather than trusting the summary) caught that a graceful-degradation deviation in Wave 2 was security-sound, and caught the premature REQUIREMENTS.md checkbox issue in Wave 3.
